step4_naming.method: Reconciliation of Step 1 (quant correlations), Step 2 (blind qualitative read, done blind to show_name), and Step 3 (between/within-show variance), plus a post-hoc boilerplate-contamination audit (see boilerplate_audit_report_500.json) that ruled out ad/sponsor copy as a driver of any pole (corpus-wide contaminated fraction 0.35%, tail fraction 0%, CFscore r=-0.086 -- MINOR, no re-run needed).

PC1.classification: specialist-IR-interview DETECTOR, not a bipolar dimension
PC1.name: Specialist geopolitics/IR-expert-interview detector
PC1.confidence: high -- AS A DETECTOR (reclassified down from 'moderate bipolar dimension')
PC1.positive_signal: A tight, legible signature: dense international-relations expert-interview discourse (Russia-Ukraine war analysis, US-Russia-China-Iran-Gulf diplomacy, NATO/ceasefire negotiation, arms control; IR-strategist vocabulary -- bandwagoning, containment, coup de main).
PC1.negative_pole_is_residual: The low pole is NOT a coherent second category -- it's residual heterogeneity ('not specialist-IR-talk'): addiction recovery, spirituality/near-death experience, sex-work conversation, celebrity interview, live-stream banter. There is no shared theme uniting the low-pole chunks beyond the absence of the high-pole signature.
PC1.quant_step1: No hypothesis feature crosses |r|>0.3; weak length signal (n_raw_words r=-0.20 -- the residual low-pole content runs longer on average, not the IR-interview content).
PC1.variance_step3: eta^2=0.372: only 5 distinct shows (of 204) supply ALL 15 high-pole extreme chunks (Russian Roulette, Foreign Affairs Interview, Glenn Diesen, Inside Story, President's Inbox) -- consistent with a detector for a small specialist clique, not a graded corpus-wide dimension.
PC1.verdict: Reclassified as a DETECTOR: high confidence that PC1 identifies 'is this one of a handful of specialist IR-interview shows,' low/no confidence that its negative pole means anything beyond 'not that.' Cleaner and more honest than calling it a moderate-confidence bipolar dimension.

PC2.name: Theoretical/academic geopolitical-economic analysis vs. Trump legal-scandal news
PC2.confidence: moderate -- most show-concentrated of the top 5 despite a clean read
PC2.high_pole: Academic/think-tank geopolitical economy: US-China rivalry via Kennan/containment framing, Soviet economic history, sanctions logic, cost-exchange military economics, AND explicit Marxist political economy (overproduction, imperialism) -- theoretical register spanning centrist wonk and heterodox-left content.
PC2.low_pole: Trump legal/scandal news: grand-jury leaks, DOJ 'weaponization' claims, E. Jean Carroll case, Epstein-files fallout, Playbook-style insider Senate gossip -- personality-driven partisan legal-drama reporting.
PC2.quant_step1: No hypothesis feature crosses |r|>0.3; weak positive lean_numeric (r=0.11) -- likely an artifact of the low pole being specific liberal Trump-accountability shows, not the high pole being conservative.
PC2.variance_step3: eta^2=0.415 -- the HIGHEST between-show fraction of the top 5; 13 outlier shows account for 38.3% of between-show SS.
PC2.verdict: Cleanest textual contrast of the concentrated pair (unlike PC1, the low pole IS a coherent second topic, not a grab-bag) -- but the numbers say this is the MOST show-bound of the five PCs read. Treat as a real but narrow content axis, not a general-purpose discourse dimension.

PC3.name: Foreign-policy/war news-briefing vs. domestic political-process & strategy discourse
PC3.confidence: high -- best-calibrated case, least show-concentrated pairing with PC5
PC3.high_pole: Domestic political science/strategy: horseshoe/four-quadrant ideology framing, neoliberalism-as-bipartisan-project, competitive authoritarianism, ranked-choice voting, campaign finance, primary-election political-science citations -- analytical panel/interview register.
PC3.low_pole: Foreign-policy/war news recitation: Iran strikes, hostage-rescue ops, Gaza/Hezbollah/Israel strikes, historical military retrospective -- daily news-anchor-brief register, ad-reads typical of daily-brief podcasts.
PC3.quant_step1: No hypothesis feature crosses |r|>0.3 (episodes_per_week r=-0.10 strongest, still weak) -- not a format/length artifact.
PC3.variance_step3: eta^2=0.271, LOWEST of the top 5: 73% of spread is within-show -- individual episodes/segments swing across this axis, not just which show. 12 distinct shows populate the high pole.
PC3.verdict: Topic + delivery-format bundled, genuinely distributed across many shows rather than a clique. Best-supported name of the five.

PC4.name: Heterodox/dissident intellectual history vs. energy & climate trade press
PC4.confidence: low-moderate -- DOWNGRADED: carries two confounds, not cleanly separable
PC4.double_confound_statement: PC4's low pole conflates energy/climate TOPIC with short-form news-brief LENGTH; topic and format cannot be cleanly separated here. Confound 1 (length): the strongest length signal of the top 5 (n_raw_words r=0.20, log_duration_sec r=0.17 -- still under the 0.3 meaningful threshold, but the largest of any top-5 PC) -- high pole runs in long-form essayistic deep-dives, low pole in short daily trade-press clips. Confound 2 (ad concentration): this was the SPECIFIC pole where sponsor ad-reads concentrated during the blind read (identical Chevron/POLITICO-Energy 'Energy Tailgate' script in 6 of 15 low-pole chunks) -- corpus-wide ad contamination cleared as MINOR (this task's audit: 0.35% corpus-wide, ad text covers only 7.6-9.4% of any one flagged chunk's words, not a majority), so the topic signal is real, but this pole specifically is where format, length, and ad-adjacency all stack on top of the topic distinction.
PC4.high_pole: Heterodox intellectual history: fascism history (Mosley, Mussolini), antisemitism history, race-theory genealogy, Eurasianism/Dugin, Maoist dialectics -- long-form essayistic register, references a named dissident-right podcaster (Thomas777).
PC4.low_pole: Energy/climate policy trade press and local governance news (POLITICO Energy, Volts) plus short local-news segments (ICE facility/DHS reporting).
PC4.variance_step3: eta^2=0.303; 6/7 distinct shows at the two poles.
PC4.verdict: Do not report this as a clean topic axis. State plainly: PC4 mixes WHAT is discussed (heterodox history vs. energy policy) with HOW LONG the format runs (essay vs. brief) and, on its low pole specifically, WHICH single-show ad-reads happen to sit there. All three are entangled; none can be attributed the effect alone.

PC5.name: Legal/constitutional case analysis vs. horse-race campaign & personality punditry
PC5.confidence: high -- clean split, least show-concentrated of the top 5
PC5.high_pole: Legal/constitutional analysis: ICC accountability, SCOTUS shadow-docket rulings, contempt doctrine, Guantanamo military commissions, qualified immunity, transgender-rights litigation -- citation-heavy legal-podcast register (Bruin, Bostock, VMI).
PC5.low_pole: Horse-race campaign chatter and political-personality gossip: 2028 primary speculation, pundit-media-figure history, fundraising numbers, Trump-rally color, Musk/Tesla business talk.
PC5.variance_step3: eta^2=0.256, tied-lowest with PC3: 12/10 distinct shows populate the two poles, no single outlier-show dominance (max share 42.3% of a modest between-show SS).
PC5.verdict: Clean, well-distributed topic contrast -- second-best-supported name of the five.

PC6_to_PC10.status: unresolved -- out of scope for this naming pass
PC6_to_PC10.reason: Not blind-read (NAMING_PCS=5 by design). Quantitative signal alone is weak and non-specific: no hypothesis feature crosses |r|>0.3 for any of PC6-10, and between-show eta^2 (0.18-0.26) doesn't distinguish a topic story from further show-identity fragmentation without a qualitative read. Naming these without reading extremes would be forcing a story the evidence doesn't support -- left honestly unresolved.

step4_naming.headline_finding: The dominant organizing axis of this embedding space is ANALYTICAL-VS-REACTIVE REGISTER, expressed across different topical domains, not any single topic itself. Every one of the five named PCs splits the same way: a high pole that is analytical, specialist, and theory-laden (legal doctrine, IR strategy, political-science frameworks, intellectual history), against a low pole that is reactive, event-driven, and personality/news-focused (horse-race gossip, daily war-briefing recitation, Trump-scandal reporting, short news-brief clips). PC3 (foreign-policy briefing vs. domestic political-process discourse) and PC5 (legal/constitutional analysis vs. horse-race punditry) are the cleanest, most broadly distributed instances of this register split -- neither is a show clique. This register axis is the MECHANISM that explains why ideology is only a minor, ~2%-variance signal (R^2=0.21): a wonky-analytical LEFT host and a wonky-analytical RIGHT host sit close together on this axis (both high/analytical), while a reactive-tabloid host of either lean sits close to the other reactive-tabloid host of the opposite lean (both low/reactive). Register cross-cuts ideology rather than tracking it, so the dimension that dominates the embedding space's variance is nearly orthogonal to the dimension DIME CFscore measures -- which is exactly why a strong ideology signal never surfaces in the top PCs. We tested and explicitly ruled out format, length, timing, and ad contamination as the actual drivers: no derived metadata feature (duration, word counts, day-of-week, guest/Q&A/live cues) crosses |Pearson r| or |Spearman r| > 0.3 against any top-10 PC (Step 1), and a dedicated post-hoc audit found ad/sponsor-boilerplate contamination is MINOR corpus-wide (0.35% of chunks, 0% in the PC-extreme tails at a >=50%-coverage bar) and uncorrelated with ideology (r=-0.086) -- so the register finding is not a mundane confound in disguise. In terms of magnitude: PC1 sits a genuine order of magnitude above the ideology axis (10.76x PC22's variance share); PC2-PC5 are smaller but still substantial gaps (5.0x-8.5x). Ideology (PC22, 0.87% of total variance) sits 15-17 PC-ranks below and 5-11x smaller than any of the five named topic/register dimensions -- a minor, secondary structure riding beneath a space whose real organizing logic is how analytically vs. reactively a podcast engages with its subject matter, independent of which side of the aisle it's on.

exact_variance_table.method: exact total variance = sum of squared entries of centered chunk embedding matrix (trace of X^T X, no eigendecomposition approximation); per-PC eigenvalue via randomized_svd(n_components=22, n_iter=4, seed=0) on the same centered matrix used throughout this task (variant=centered, target=500).
exact_variance_table.verdict: PC1 is a genuine order-of-magnitude gap over the ideology axis (10.76x, PC1=9.39% vs PC22=0.87% of total variance). PC2-PC5 are smaller gaps that do NOT support 'order of magnitude': PC2=8.52x, PC3=7.19x, PC4=5.45x, PC5=5.04x. Corrected headline language: 'PC1 is an order of magnitude larger; PC2-PC5 are roughly 5-8.5x larger' -- not a blanket order-of-magnitude claim across all five.
